key_insight: Token usage in LLM agents is highly variable and cannot be reliably estimated upfront because each tool call and new observation changes the future context size. TokenCast tackles this by forecasting consumption as the run unfolds, enabling adaptive prediction instead of a single static estimate.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the difficulty of predicting total token consumption for LLM agent tasks before or during execution. Traditional fixed-cost estimates fail because agent trajectories diverge across runs and context growth makes later calls increasingly expensive.
method: Learns a composable cost model that estimates token use across an agent's multi-step execution.
Updates predictions dynamically as intermediate results, tool feedback, and context expansion accumulate.
Models token consumption as a run-time forecasting problem rather than a one-shot prediction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps with budgeting, latency planning, and infrastructure sizing for agentic systems. More accurate token forecasts can reduce cost overruns and improve deployment reliability for LLM workflows.
visual_elements: A step-by-step agent workflow diagram showing context growth over time
A line chart comparing predicted vs. actual token consumption across runs
A side-by-side illustration of static estimation vs. dynamic forecasting
Icons for tools, feedback loops, and token stacks to show cost accumulation
paper_title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution
paper_authors: Chaoqian Ouyang, Ling Yue, Libin Zheng, Huanghui Guo, Shengxiang Xu
